adversarial_framing_check_notes: Lead Regional story is a Houthi missile strike on a Saudi vessel in the Red Sea (NYT, 17 Aug 2026) - a geopolitical/security context, so the check is applicable. Checked Al Jazeera (Qatari state-funded), Middle East Eye (Qatar-linked), and Iranian state media (Press TV/Tehran Times/Tasnim) for in-window framing casting Saudi Arabia as aggressor/oppressor. Finding: all IN-WINDOW (17-18 Aug) eligible coverage frames the Iran-backed Houthis as the aggressor and Saudi Arabia as the party under attack (sympathetic to Saudi, not adversarial). The adversarial-toward-Saudi framing (Houthis' 'oppressive siege'/'an eye for an eye' retaliation narrative; Saudi-led coalition airstrike criticism) appears only in OUT-OF-WINDOW articles (20-22 Jul, 9-12 Aug 2026) and historical pieces (2018/2022/2024), which fail the in-window gate. No in-window eligible article frames Saudi adversarially on this event; therefore no Negative Articles item is generated from the adversarial-framing check.
negative_notes: Every negative theme and all 9 watchdog NGOs were searched. All negative-for-Saudi material found (record executions, migrant/labour abuse, sportswashing, Vision 2030 downsizing, press-freedom rankings, war-driven tourism/investment reputation risk) is OUT-OF-WINDOW (Jan-Jul 2026 or earlier, or undated NGO landing/annual-report pages) or from EXCLUDED/weak sources (Times of Israel - Israeli outlet, hard exclusion; Sanad/MEDC/eturbonews advocacy or trade blogs). AGBI's 'Houthi strikes threaten Saudi investment plans' (negative-for-Saudi, credible) is dated 11 Aug 2026, outside the 24h window. No in-window, eligible, non-excluded Negative Article exists for this edition; Negative Articles is legitimately empty per the Stage 5 minimum-coverage ladder.
